title: A Rivergate for the Horizon
premise: Marguerite Almeida, a storm chaser drowning in debt to the Vantablack Club—a syndicate of wealthy 'optimists' who fund disasters like investments—takes a salvage contract to find the Halcyon Reach expedition, silent for three weeks on the Sereno River. What he finds is a crew alive but sworn to silence: they've located a pre-calving ice archive that could rewrite climate history and bankrupt half the Club's portfolio. Marguerite must ferry them home through narrowing meltwater channels before the calving season seals the route, all while lying to his creditors, his radio handlers, and the woman he loves who is aboard against orders. He gets the expedition—and the truth—through the pass in the final hours of open water, then chooses truth over loyalty by broadcasting the archive, freeing himself from debt at the cost of everything he was.
about_author: Paloma Oyelaran is a former river guide who spent six seasons on glacial meltwater routes before turning to fiction full-time. She writes adventure novels about people whose professions require them to lie beautifully.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. We meet him mid-storm chase in Oklahoma, measuring his life in odometer readings, then cutting to the Vantablack Club's velvet back room where his debt is renegotiated into a salvage job. Emotional beat: a man who has made speed into an identity being handed a destination he can't outrun.

chapters.title: The Silence on Channel Nine
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The Halcyon Reach expedition goes quiet on the radio during a routine check-in; Marguerite, contracted as their supply pilot, is ordered upstream alone. He packs instruments he doesn't understand and lies to his sister about where he's going. Beat: dread disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: Sereno Headwaters
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The river journey begins—narrowing channels, abandoned survey markers, a drowned research station. He finds evidence the expedition passed through in a hurry, leaving gear behind deliberately. Beat: the landscape itself becomes an antagonist, beautiful and withholding.

chapters.title: What the Ice Keeps
chapters.summary: Ines Okonkwo's POV, the expedition's glaciologist. Flashback to the discovery: a blue-ice archive holding sixty thousand years of atmospheric record, and the crew's vote to go dark until they can verify it. Ines voted for silence; she isn't sure she still believes in it. Beat: guilt wearing the mask of principle.

chapters.title: The Woman Against Orders
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. He reaches the expedition's last known camp and finds Tomas Reyes—the man he was sent to retrieve—alive, armed, and refusing rescue. Their standoff reveals the first crack: someone else knows about the archive, someone who isn't part of the crew. Beat: loyalty revealed as a contested territory.

chapters.title: Debt Collectors Upstream
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A second boat appears on the river—Vantablack men, ostensibly 'support contractors,' led by the affable and terrifying Mr. Latch. They know more than they should. Marguerite must decide what to tell them over shared campfire coffee. Beat: the first outright lie, told well enough to hate himself for.

chapters.title: Halcyon Reach
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. He finally reaches the main expedition camp hidden in a lateral valley: eleven survivors, a functioning camp, and a wall of data. Among them is Dr. Amara Voss, the expedition's medic—his former partner, the love he left seven years ago. Beat: reunion as ambush.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Weather
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. She recounts their breakup and her reasons for joining an expedition that would vanish. Now she watches Marguerite calculate exits and recognizes the old pattern: a man who loves at highway speed. Beat: tenderness sharpened into accusation.

chapters.title: The Archive Vote
chapters.summary: Expedition leader Dr. Halloran's POV. The crew debates whether to trust Marguerite with the full truth of the ice archive—data that proves a coming collapse the Club has been betting against. Halloran argues for silence; the vote is split. Beat: democracy under pressure.

chapters.title: Latch's Ledger
chapters.summary: Mr. Latch's POV. The Club's man logs his assets: the river, the crew, and Marguerite himself, itemized with cheerful precision. He radios home that the salvage is proceeding 'on schedule,' meaning the expedition will not come back. Beat: villainy as bookkeeping.

chapters.title: Radio Silence, Broken
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite secretly repairs the expedition's transmitter, torn between calling his handlers (betraying the crew) or staying dark (voiding his debt contract and endangering his sister, whom the Club holds as collateral). Beat: the loyalty-versus-truth theme made literal in a single switch.

chapters.title: Calving Season Opens
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The glacier begins to calve early; the downstream route will close within days. The window that justified all the secrecy is now the thing killing them. Ines realizes the archive must move or be lost forever. Beat: nature collapsing the moral argument.

chapters.title: The Bargain at the Moraine
chapters.summary: Marguerite and Amara's alternating POV. On a night hike along the moraine, Marguerite tells Amara about the debt, the sister, the trap. She offers him the one thing he can't take: her testimony that some truths are worth bankruptcy. Beat: love re-entering as a force, not a memory.

chapters.title: Loading the Blue Ice
chapters.summary: Halloran's POV. The crew cores, packs, and seals the archive samples for transport while Latch's men watch from the ridge. Halloran makes a private decision: if the mission fails, the samples burn with him. Beat: duty curdling into martyrdom.

chapters.title: First Rapids
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The flotilla launches—three boats, eleven scientists, forty pounds of ice core, and two Vantablack 'escorts.' The river runs high and hostile. Marguerite reads water he's never seen and lies to Latch about the route. Beat: competence as a form of resistance.

chapters.title: The Drowned Station Revisited
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Passing the ruined research station from Chapter 3, they discover Latch's men have been there before—years ago. The Club always knew what the ice held. Amara confronts Marguerite with the implication: he was never hired to rescue anyone. Beat: betrayal reframed; every prior chapter shifts color.

chapters.title: Mutiny at the Confluence
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV, rotating paragraphs. At the confluence, Latch attempts to seize the samples and the crew fractures—some want to trade the archive for safe passage. Marguerite, caught between both sides, chooses the crew publicly for the first time. Beat: the point of no return.

chapters.title: What Marguerite Owes
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Captured briefly by Latch, Marguerite is offered full debt forgiveness and his sister's safety in exchange for the cores' location. He gives up something real instead—a coordinates cache that is partly true—to buy time. Beat: sacrifice without heroism; the cost priced honestly.

chapters.title: The Pass
chapters.summary: Marguerite and Ines's POV. The final run through the calving corridor: ice walls detonating on both sides, boats separated, Halloran lost holding the rear. Ines navigates by memory of a channel she surveyed as a student. Beat: climax—pure velocity, grief, and skill fused.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Through the last open water, Marguerite makes his choice: he transmits the archive's summary data openly, to every listener on the band, before the Club can bury it. His debt becomes worthless; his protection with it. Beat: truth chosen over loyalty, at maximum price.

chapters.title: Downriver
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The survivors reach the delta as the route closes behind them. Latch is gone, his ledger ruined; Halloran is mourned; the sister is freed by the Club's collapse. Marguerite and Amara stand on the shore with nothing owed and nothing certain. Beat: exhaustion transfigured into beginning.

chapters.title: A Rivergate for the Horizon
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, epilogue. Months later, Marguerite drives slowly for the first time in his life, the published archive riding in the passenger seat. He measures the trip in hours now, not miles, and lets the horizon stay where it belongs—a gate, not an escape. Beat: resolution; a man finally at rest inside time.
